messages:
Maria: Ran a 60s nsys trace on canary for the KV-cache regression. Quick summary — when cache hit rate drops ~30% we see a sharp kernel-time spike. Attn_forward and kv_cache_lookup are top time sinks; kv_evict_loop shows up intermittently but is expensive when it does. Posting raw snippets + perfetto link below.

perf-bot: Auto-summary: top kernels by total time -> attn_fwd 42.3%, kv_cache_lookup 24.1%, kv_evict_loop 18.7%, softmax 6.5%, memcpy_h2d 3.2%.

Dima: Can you paste the nsys top10 lines (kernel name / total time / SM util / regs / shared) so we can rank suspects? Also which sequence length distribution triggered this?

Maria: Paste from nsys top kernels:```
# name                     total_time(ms)  calls  avg(ms)  sm_eff(%)  regs  shared_kB
attn_forward               2543.1          3200   0.794     78.4       84    64
kv_cache_lookup            1448.6          9800   0.148     62.1       72    12
kv_evict_loop             1126.9           430   2.621     34.2       96    48
softmax                    87.1           4300   0.020     71.5       40    0
memcpy_h2d                 19.4            12    1.617     n/a        n/a   n/a
```
Perfetto trace: https://perfetto.dev/trace/host/abcd1234 (link to timeline with kernel swimlanes).

Ash: kv_evict_loop looks destructive — is it a device kernel or a host fallback loop? Any host<->device syncs around its launches?

Maria: It's a device kernel. nvprof shows launches in short bursts right after big cache-miss storms. Snippet of launch timestamps (ns):```
launch 0: 1612345678900000  kernel kv_cache_lookup
launch 1: 1612345678954000  kernel kv_cache_lookup
launch 2: 1612345679001000  kernel kv_evict_loop
launch 3: 1612345679004500  kernel kv_evict_loop
```
We also see small memcpy_h2d spikes preceding evict loops (likely metadata updates).

Lee: Could batching heuristic be amplifying misses? If many short sequences bubble through, prefix cache TTL might be too short and cause repeated evicts. Which batch policy was used?

Maria: Run used policy `dynamic_small_batch` with token_threshold=128 and aggressive_eviction=true. Recalled that `burst-batch-agg` historically reduced evictions for similar traces.

Dima: Actionable proposal: run A/B traces: (A) keep current runtime but enable prefixTTL=0.5s to allow short reuse; (B) run with `burst-batch-agg`. Capture nsys + SM-util heatmaps. Also add nvprof counters for warp_serialize and l2_hit_rate. That should isolate whether eviction cost or kernel inefficiency dominates.

Maria: I'll schedule two 60s traces and include the extra counters. Will also capture per-kernel stall reasons (mempipe vs exec). cc @perf-bot.

perf-bot: :thumbsup: Traces queued as perf-job-9876 (A) and perf-job-9877 (B). Results will be uploaded to /perf/traces/kv-shadow-probe/.

Ash: Add a short experiment to toggle kv-prefetch (speculative load of next-token KV) — if prefetch reduces kv_cache_lookup hotness and evictions, that's a good signal for a batching-level fix. Also add a run with quantized kernels to see asm-level differences.

Maria: Good call — adding prefetch toggle and a quantized run. Will report comparative top-kernel deltas and a ranked suspect list (time %, SM util, regs) once traces complete.

Dima: One more ask: include per-SM occupancy histogram in uploads. If kv_cache_lookup shows many low-occupancy bins, that's a strong signal to optimize kernel launch config (warps/regs/shared).

Maria: Noted. I'll include occupancy hist and link the heatmap. Expect first results in ~90m.
